annotations.title: JSON Schema validation of a document

description: Validate a JSON document against a JSON Schema and report every violation with its JSON Pointer path and the keyword that failed. Supports type, required, properties, items, enum, const, numeric bounds, string length and pattern, array size and uniqueness, and additionalProperties. Choose this when you have a concrete JSON document and a JSON Schema and need every violation located by JSON Pointer path and failing keyword. Do not choose this when you need a validator module for your own service (use webhook-payload-validation), or when the schema relies on $ref, allOf, anyOf or oneOf, which this documented subset does not evaluate. Example requests: Validate this JSON payload against my schema and list the failures. | Which fields in this webhook payload violate the schema? | Check this API response against its JSON Schema.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

content.description: The customer's input.json, as text. Supported: JSON. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

inputs.title: JSON Schema validation of a document

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_json_schema_validation

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.
